Anchorgrounded RAG with verified citations
Retrieval · LLM evaluation · shipped

A retrieval system over vLLM's documentation that refuses to answer when it cannot cite a source. Every claim is traced to the span it cites, and claims naming a CLI flag are checked against vLLM's actual source tree.

  • Corpus. vLLM cloned at a pinned commit. Docs, README and public docstrings parsed, every document tagged with version and commit so staleness stays detectable.
  • Chunking. Two strategies written to the database at once so they can be queried identically: a 512-token sliding window, and a structure-aware splitter that never splits a fenced code block.
  • Index. bge-small-en-v1.5 embeddings into pgvector with an HNSW index, Postgres full-text vector in the same row, so hybrid search is one SQL statement.
  • Retrieve. Dense and sparse top-k fused by reciprocal rank fusion, then reranked by a bge-reranker-base cross-encoder over the shortlist.
  • Ground. Claims split from the answer, scored against the cited span, checkable names routed to the symbol oracle, then the abstention policy applied.
  • Serve. Qwen2.5-3B under 4-bit AWQ quantization through vLLM, load-tested with k6 to saturation at 12.5 req/s with zero failures across 1,080 requests.

A measurement bug, not a model bug. The first results table folded two failure modes into one column and reported a 37% hallucination rate. Split apart, claims citing a contradicting span versus claims citing nothing, the strict rate is 1 in 496. Three of the four worst bugs in this project were in the measurement, and each would have produced a plausible number that was wrong.

Where vLLM's documentation actually lives. Engine arguments are documented as attribute docstrings, which ast.get_docstring cannot see because they belong to no function or class. That is 532 field descriptions in vllm/config/ alone, missing from both the doc sources and a naive docstring pass.

Hallucination-Aware Memory Immune System
Agentic AI · LLM reliability · shipped

A real-time auditing layer for LLM long-term memory. It detects self-contradiction, user-induced false beliefs, staleness and unsourced fabrication at write time, quarantining corrupted entries before they reach downstream responses.

  • Shipped as an installable MCP server with a three-tier validation pipeline, ordered cheapest first: lexicon and regex, then value comparison, then LLM adjudication.
  • Benchmarked against a no-audit baseline at 1.00 precision and recall, answering 13 of 13 downstream questions correctly against 1 of 13 for the naive store.

SAGESmall Business Autonomous Growth Engine
Multi-agent systems · reinforcement learning · complete

A closed-loop multi-agent system for small business operations. Five agents coordinate over Redis pub/sub, and the orchestration layer learns which cross-agent signals are worth acting on.

  • An IRL-based owner preference model with 30-day rolling drift detection, cutting preference-adaptation time from 18 days to 7 under simulated preference shifts.
  • Full React frontend, presented at a departmental lightning talk.

LLM Inference Profilingquantization and KV cache dynamics
GPU performance · roofline analysis

An empirical test of the memory-bandwidth-bound hypothesis in autoregressive inference, using roofline analysis across FP32, FP16 and INT8 on UMD's A100 cluster and a local RTX 5070 Ti.

  • Three controlled experiments: precision tradeoffs, KV cache growth against prefill and decode latency, and batch size saturation, measuring arithmetic intensity, bandwidth utilization and token throughput.
  • INT8 ran slower than FP16, because BitsAndBytes dequantization overhead exceeded the bandwidth saved at this model size.
